questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was crucial that my destination was known to have a good student environment where it was easy to make new friends. Furthermore, it was also important that the university had a good reputation in regard to academic opportunities.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easier to find the information I needed when I arrived than from back home. I could however have wished for even more information from the university as it was quite hard to find out how to choose courses, and it was only made clear after the courses had begun.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Information on how to sign up for courses. Information on how to become part of the student environment.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very hard and very expensive. It is not possible to find good and cheap housing except if you know someone living in Bologna already. Prepare yourself to spend at least €650 for a room in a shared flat.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Bologna is quite a small city, so no matter what, you are never far from campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
It was a guessing game where the university kept on changing what courses we could sign up for as students. As a Master's student, I did not have that many issues as my home university already only allowed me to do Master's courses. One of my courses was however moved to the following semester without me being notified - and after my host institution had approved that course in my learning agreement.
Furthermore, my friends who were Bachelor's students struggled a lot with finding courses that they were allowed to take, and there was almost no information online so they had to show up and ask the professors. This meant that they missed out on a lot of classes on the first weeks of the courses they ended up being allowed to take.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: No help seemed available except for showing up and talking to each professor.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was lucky and succeeded in registering for 3 out of the 4 classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you are a BA student, do not expect to be able to do the classes you have been offered from Bologna when you initially signed up.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the MA courses in UNIBO were equivalent to BA courses at UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: We had to participate much more in classes, memorise more than being critical, and we also had many more exams than at UCPH (the exams were however easier).

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: China in Africa, History & International Relations of the Middle East, Politics of Collective Violence and Terrorism & Counterterrorism.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Politics of Collective Violence was recommendable course as the professor was really cool.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to pay for a second SIM card the last two months, as the Danish ones stop working after being outside of Denmark for 3-4 months.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Food in supermarkets were way more expensive than expected. You had to go outside the city walls to find lower prices than in Denmark.
Housing was also more expensive than expected - especially compared to the quality of the housing.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I did not participate in any.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did not participate in any.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Bologna is very well-connected by train. I recommend to go and explore the nearby cities.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy. As a Northern Europeaner you however had to have a little patience as everything happens slower and a bit more bureaucratically.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to people in class.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The professors do not see the students as their equals as they do at UCPH. They found it very important to address them in the proper manner, and if you failed to do it, some of them became quite aggressive.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The restaurant culture as well as meeting up culture drinking a cheap coffee are amazing.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Find someone who has been on exchange in Bologna and ask them how they found housing, be patient with signing up for courses, and enjoy the amazing food culture.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Reach out to students who have already been on exchange at your host institution.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The amazing people I met.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Living in a very small apartment with six other exchange students who were very young.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
